sanskrit: saṃjayaivaṃgate prāṇāṃs tyaktum icchāmi māciram stokaṃ hy api na paśyāmi phalaṃ jīvitadhāraṇe
english: O Sañjaya, now that things have come to this pass, I wish to give up my life without delay, for I see not even the slightest benefit in continuing to live.

sanskrit: taṃ tathāvādinaṃ dīnaṃ vilapantaṃ mahīpatim gāvalgaṇir idaṃ dhīmān mahārthaṃ vākyam abravīt
english: To that king, despondent and lamenting thus, the wise son of Gavalgaṇa — Sañjaya — spoke these weighty and momentous words.

sanskrit: śrutavān asi vai rājño mahotsāhān mahābalān dvaipāyanasya vadato nāradasya ca dhīmataḥ
english: You have heard, O king, about those rulers of immense enterprise and great might, as recounted by the sage Dvaipāyana and the wise Nārada.

sanskrit: mahatsu rājavaṃśeṣu guṇaiḥ samuditeṣu ca jātān divyāstraviduṣaḥ śakrapratimatejasaḥ
english: Born in the greatest of royal lineages, distinguished by every virtue, versed in celestial weapons, and equal in splendour to Indra himself —

sanskrit: dharmeṇa pṛthivīṃ jitvā yajñair iṣṭvāptadakṣiṇaiḥ asmiṃl loke yaśaḥ prāpya tataḥ kālavaśaṃ gatāḥ
english: — having conquered the earth by righteousness, having performed sacrifices with lavish gifts of honour, having won glory in this world — they too in the end came under the dominion of time.

sanskrit: vainyaṃ mahārathaṃ vīraṃ sṛñjayaṃ jayatāṃ varam suhotraṃ rantidevaṃ ca kakṣīvantaṃ tathauśijam
english: Vainya the great warrior, heroic Sṛñjaya foremost among conquerors, Suhotra, Rantideva, Kakṣīvān the son of Uśij —

sanskrit: bāhlīkaṃ damanaṃ śaibyaṃ śaryātim ajitaṃ jitam viśvāmitram amitraghnam ambarīṣaṃ mahābalam
english: — Bāhlika, Damana, Śaibya, Śaryāti, the unconquerable who was yet conquered, Viśvāmitra the slayer of enemies, mighty Ambarīṣa —

sanskrit: maruttaṃ manum ikṣvākuṃ gayaṃ bharatam eva ca rāmaṃ dāśarathiṃ caiva śaśabinduṃ bhagīratham
english: — Marutta, Manu, Ikṣvāku, Gaya, and Bharata himself, Rāma the son of Daśaratha, Śaśabindu, Bhagīratha —

sanskrit: yayātiṃ śubhakarmāṇaṃ devair yo yājitaḥ svayam caityayūpāṅkitā bhūmir yasyeyaṃ savanākarā
english: — Yayāti of auspicious deeds, for whom the gods themselves served as officiating priests, and whose whole earth became marked with sacrificial posts and filled with the sounds of soma-pressings —

sanskrit: iti rājñāṃ caturviṃśan nāradena surarṣiṇā putraśokābhitaptāya purā śaibyāya kīrtitāḥ
english: — these twenty-four kings were thus enumerated long ago by the divine sage Nārada to Śaibya, who was consumed by grief for his son.

sanskrit: tebhyaś cānye gatāḥ pūrvaṃ rājāno balavattarāḥ mahārathā mahātmānaḥ sarvaiḥ samuditā guṇaiḥ
english: And before them still others passed away — kings even mightier, great warriors, noble souls, endowed with every virtue.

sanskrit: pūruḥ kurur yaduḥ śūro viṣvagaśvo mahādhṛtiḥ anenā yuvanāśvaś ca kakutstho vikramī raghuḥ
english: Pūru, Kuru, Yadu, Śūra, Viṣvagaśva, Mahādhṛti, Anenā, Yuvanāśva, Kākutstha, Vikramī, Raghu —

sanskrit: vijitī vītihotraś ca bhavaḥ śveto bṛhadguruḥ uśīnaraḥ śatarathaḥ kaṅko duliduho drumaḥ
english: — Vijitī, Vītihotra, Bhava, Śveta, Bṛhadguru, Uśīnara, Śataratha, Kaṅka, Duliduh, Druma —

sanskrit: dambhodbhavaḥ paro venaḥ sagaraḥ saṃkṛtir nimiḥ ajeyaḥ paraśuḥ puṇḍraḥ śambhur devāvṛdho 'naghaḥ
english: — Dambhodbhava, Para, Vena, Sagara, Saṃkṛti, Nimi, Ajeya, Paraśu, Puṇḍra, Śambhu, Devāvṛdha the sinless —

sanskrit: devāhvayaḥ supratimaḥ supratīko bṛhadrathaḥ mahotsāho vinītātmā sukratur naiṣadho nalaḥ
english: — Devāhvaya, Supratima, Supratīka, Bṛhadratha, Mahotsāha, Vinītātmā, Sukratu, Nala the lord of Niṣadha —

sanskrit: satyavrataḥ śāntabhayaḥ sumitraḥ subalaḥ prabhuḥ jānujaṅgho 'naraṇyo 'rkaḥ priyabhṛtyaḥ śubhavrataḥ
english: — Satyavrata, Śāntabhaya, Sumitrā, Subala the mighty lord, Jānujaṅgha, Anaraṇya, Arka, Priyabhṛtya, Śubhavrata —

sanskrit: balabandhur nirāmardaḥ ketuśṛṅgo bṛhadbalaḥ dhṛṣṭaketur bṛhatketur dīptaketur nirāmayaḥ
english: — Balabandhu, Nirāmarda, Ketuśṛṅga, Bṛhadbala, Dhṛṣṭaketu, Bṛhatketu, Dīptaketu, Nirāmaya —

sanskrit: avikṣit prabalo dhūrtaḥ kṛtabandhur dṛḍheṣudhiḥ mahāpurāṇaḥ saṃbhāvyaḥ pratyaṅgaḥ parahā śrutiḥ
english: — Avikṣit, Prabala, Dhūrta, Kṛtabandhu, Dṛḍheṣudhi, Mahāpurāṇa, Saṃbhāvya, Pratyaṅga, Parahā, Śruti —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavaḥ śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ śrūyante 'yutaśaś cānye saṃkhyātāś cāpi padmaśaḥ
english: These and countless others are heard of — hundreds, thousands, ten thousands, and still more counted in the hundreds of millions.

sanskrit: hitvā suvipulān bhogān buddhimanto mahābalāḥ rājāno nidhanaṃ prāptās tava putrair mahattamāḥ
english: Wise and mighty kings who had renounced the most vast pleasures — they too met their deaths, surpassing even your sons in greatness.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ divyāni karmāṇi vikramas tyāga eva ca māhātmyam api cāstikyaṃ satyatā śaucam ārjavam
english: Whose deeds were celestial, whose valour and generosity, whose nobility of soul, reverence for the sacred, truthfulness, purity and straightforwardness —

sanskrit: vidvadbhiḥ kathyate loke purāṇaiḥ kavisattamaiḥ sarvarddhiguṇasaṃpannās te cāpi nidhanaṃ gatāḥ
english: — are celebrated in the world by scholars, by ancient sages and the greatest of poets — even those endowed with the full wealth of all virtues passed away.

sanskrit: tava putrā durātmānaḥ prataptāś caiva manyunā lubdhā durvṛttabhūyiṣṭhā na tāñ śocitum arhasi
english: Your sons were evil-minded, consumed by wrath, greedy, and predominantly ill-behaved — you should not grieve for them.

sanskrit: śrutavān asi medhāvī buddhimān prājñasaṃmataḥ yeṣāṃ śāstrānugā buddhir na te muhyanti bhārata
english: You are learned, O Bhārata, intelligent and wise, esteemed by the wise; those whose understanding follows the scriptures are not deluded.

sanskrit: nigrahānugrahau cāpi viditau te narādhipa nātyantam evānuvṛttiḥ śrūyate putrarakṣaṇe
english: Both punishment and favour are well known to you, O lord of men; it is taught that one should not be utterly indulgent in shielding one's sons.

sanskrit: bhavitavyaṃ tathā tac ca nātaḥ śocitum arhasi daivaṃ prajñāviśeṣeṇa ko nivartitum arhati
english: What had to be has come to pass — you should not grieve over it. Who, however superior his wisdom, is able to turn back fate?

sanskrit: vidhātṛvihitaṃ mārgaṃ na kaś cid ativartate kālamūlam idaṃ sarvaṃ bhāvābhāvau sukhāsukhe
english: None transgresses the path ordained by the Creator. All this — existence and non-existence, pleasure and pain — has time as its root.

sanskrit: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharati prajāḥ nirdahantaṃ prajāḥ kālaṃ kālaḥ śamayate punaḥ
english: Time ripens all beings; time dissolves all creatures; and time again pacifies that same time which burns the people to ashes.

sanskrit: kālo vikurute bhāvān sarvāṃl loke śubhāśubhān kālaḥ saṃkṣipate sarvāḥ prajā visṛjate punaḥ kālaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu caraty avidhṛtaḥ samaḥ
english: Time transforms all conditions in the world, both auspicious and inauspicious; time contracts all creatures and once more releases them; time moves among all beings, unobstructed and impartial.

sanskrit: atītānāgatā bhāvā ye ca vartanti sāṃpratam tān kālanirmitān buddhvā na saṃjñāṃ hātum arhasi
english: Past conditions, future ones, and those which exist at present — understanding that all are fashioned by time, you should not abandon your composure.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca atropaniṣadaṃ puṇyāṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt bhāratādhyayanāt puṇyād api pādam adhīyataḥ śraddadhānasya pūyante sarvapāpāny aśeṣataḥ
english: The Sūta said: Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana declared this holy secret teaching here — that even one who studies with faith a single verse of the meritorious Bhārata is purified of all sins without remainder.

sanskrit: devarṣayo hy atra puṇyā brahmarājarṣayas tathā kīrtyante śubhakarmāṇas tathā yakṣamahoragāḥ
english: For in this text are celebrated the holy divine sages, as well as the brahmarṣis and rājarṣis of auspicious deeds, and likewise the yakṣas and great serpents.

sanskrit: bhagavān vāsudevaś ca kīrtyate 'tra sanātanaḥ sa hi satyam ṛtaṃ caiva pavitraṃ puṇyam eva ca
english: The eternal Lord Vāsudeva too is celebrated here; for he is truth and righteousness, the pure and the holy.

sanskrit: śāśvataṃ brahma paramaṃ dhruvaṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam yasya divyāni karmāṇi kathayanti manīṣiṇaḥ
english: He is the eternal Brahman supreme, the unchanging and everlasting light, whose divine deeds the wise declare.

sanskrit: asat sat sad asac caiva yasmād devāt pravartate saṃtatiś ca pravṛttiś ca janma mṛtyuḥ punarbhavaḥ
english: From that God proceed the non-existent, the existent, and also both the existent and non-existent together — the continuity of creation, its ongoing activity, birth, death, and rebirth.

sanskrit: adhyātmaṃ śrūyate yac ca pañcabhūtaguṇātmakam avyaktādi paraṃ yac ca sa eva parigīyate
english: And what is heard regarding the Self — that which consists of the qualities of the five elements, and that supreme reality beginning with the Unmanifest — he alone is hymned as all of that.

sanskrit: yat tad yativarā yuktā dhyānayogabalānvitāḥ pratibimbam ivādarśe paśyanty ātmany avasthitam
english: That which the best of ascetics, intent in meditation and possessed of the power of yoga, behold as dwelling in the self — like a reflection in a mirror — is he.

sanskrit: śraddadhānaḥ sadodyuktaḥ satyadharmaparāyaṇaḥ āsevann imam adhyāyaṃ naraḥ pāpāt pramucyate
english: A person who is faithful, ever diligent, devoted to truth and righteousness, and who regularly studies this chapter is freed from sin.

sanskrit: anukramaṇim adhyāyaṃ bhāratasyemam āditaḥ āstikaḥ satataṃ śṛṇvan na kṛcchreṣv avasīdati
english: The believer who continually hears this table-of-contents chapter of the Bhārata from the beginning never sinks in adversities.

sanskrit: ubhe saṃdhye japan kiṃ cit sadyo mucyeta kilbiṣāt anukramaṇyā yāvat syād ahnā rātryā ca saṃcitam
english: Reciting even a little of it at both twilight junctions, one is immediately freed from whatever transgression has been accumulated through the day and the night.

sanskrit: bhāratasya vapur hy etat satyaṃ cāmṛtam eva ca navanītaṃ yathā dadhno dvipadāṃ brāhmaṇo yathā
english: For this is the very body of the Bhārata — both true and immortal; as butter is the essence of curds, so is the brahmin the essence among two-footed beings —

sanskrit: hradānām udadhiḥ śreṣṭho gaur variṣṭhā catuṣpadām yathaitāni variṣṭhāni tathā bhāratam ucyate
english: — as the ocean is supreme among lakes and the cow is the highest among four-footed beings, so in the same way the Bhārata is called the most excellent.

sanskrit: yaś cainaṃ śrāvayec chrāddhe brāhmaṇān pādam antataḥ akṣayyam annapānaṃ tat pitṝṃs tasyopatiṣṭhati
english: Whoever causes even a single verse of it to be recited to brahmins at a śrāddha ceremony — inexhaustible food and drink stands ready for his ancestors.

sanskrit: itihāsapurāṇābhyāṃ vedaṃ samupabṛṃhayet bibhety alpaśrutād vedo mām ayaṃ pratariṣyati
english: One should supplement the Veda with the Itihāsa and Purāṇa; the Veda fears the poorly-learned, thinking: 'This person will cross me over wrongly.'

sanskrit: kārṣṇaṃ vedam imaṃ vidvāñ śrāvayitvārtham aśnute bhrūṇahatyākṛtaṃ cāpi pāpaṃ jahyān na saṃśayaḥ
english: The learned one who causes this Veda of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana to be recited attains its fruit, and sheds even the sin incurred by the slaying of an embryo — without doubt.

sanskrit: ya imaṃ śucir adhyāyaṃ paṭhet parvaṇi parvaṇi adhītaṃ bhārataṃ tena kṛtsnaṃ syād iti me matiḥ
english: Whoever, with a pure heart, recites this chapter at every fortnightly occasion — by him the entire Bhārata may be considered as having been studied, in my judgement.

sanskrit: yaś cemaṃ śṛṇuyān nityam ārṣaṃ śraddhāsamanvitaḥ sa dīrgham āyuḥ kīrtiṃ ca svargatiṃ cāpnuyān naraḥ
english: The person who daily hears this seer-composed text with faith will attain long life, fame, and passage to heaven.

sanskrit: catvāra ekato vedā bhārataṃ caikam ekataḥ samāgataiḥ surarṣibhis tulām āropitaṃ purā mahattve ca gurutve ca dhriyamāṇaṃ tato 'dhikam
english: On one side were placed the four Vedas together, and the Bhārata alone on the other side, when the divine sages assembled and weighed them of old; in greatness and in weight the Bhārata was found to be the heavier.

sanskrit: mahattvād bhāravattvāc ca mahābhāratam ucyate niruktam asya yo veda sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate
english: Because of its greatness and because of its weightiness, it is called the Mahābhārata; one who knows its true etymology is freed from all sins.

sanskrit: tapo na kalko 'dhyayanaṃ na kalkaḥ; svābhāviko vedavidhir na kalkaḥ prasahya vittāharaṇaṃ na kalkas; tāny eva bhāvopahatāni kalkaḥ
english: Austerity is not impurity, nor is study impurity; the natural observance of Vedic duty is not impurity, nor is forceful acquisition of wealth impurity — but those same acts, when tainted by evil intention, become impurity.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ samantapañcakam iti yad uktaṃ sūtanandana etat sarvaṃ yathānyāyaṃ śrotum icchāmahe vayam
english: The sages said: O son of the sūta, you have mentioned a place called Samantapañcaka — we wish to hear all about it fully and in due order.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca śuśrūṣā yadi vo viprā bruvataś ca kathāḥ śubhāḥ samantapañcakākhyaṃ ca śrotum arhatha sattamāḥ
english: The Sūta said: If you, O brāhmaṇas, desire to hear my words and these auspicious tales, then listen, O best of the twice-born, to the account called Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: tretādvāparayoḥ saṃdhau rāmaḥ śastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ asakṛt pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ jaghānāmarṣacoditaḥ
english: At the junction of the Tretā and Dvāpara ages, Rāma — the foremost of those who bear arms — driven by wrath, repeatedly slaughtered the earthly warrior class.

sanskrit: sa sarvaṃ kṣatram utsādya svavīryeṇānaladyutiḥ samantapañcake pañca cakāra rudhirahradān
english: Having extirpated all the kṣatriyas by his own might, blazing like fire, he made five lakes of blood at Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: sa teṣu rudhirāmbhassu hradeṣu krodhamūrcchitaḥ pitṝn saṃtarpayām āsa rudhireṇeti naḥ śrutam
english: In those blood-filled lakes, overcome with rage, he satisfied his ancestors with blood — so we have heard.

sanskrit: atharcīkādayo 'bhyetya pitaro brāhmaṇarṣabham taṃ kṣamasveti siṣidhus tataḥ sa virarāma ha
english: Then the ancestors, headed by Ṛcīka, came to that bull among brāhmaṇas and restrained him saying: 'Forgive, forgive!' — and thereupon he desisted.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samīpe yo deśo hradānāṃ rudhirāmbhasām samantapañcakam iti puṇyaṃ tatparikīrtitam
english: The holy region near those blood-filled lakes is celebrated as Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: yena liṅgena yo deśo yuktaḥ samupalakṣyate tenaiva nāmnā taṃ deśaṃ vācyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ
english: The wise declare that the region which is identified and distinguished by a particular mark should be named according to that very mark.

sanskrit: antare caiva saṃprāpte kalidvāparayor abhūt samantapañcake yuddhaṃ kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ
english: And in the interval that arrived between the Dvāpara and Kali ages, the great battle of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava armies took place at Samantapañcaka.

sanskrit: tasmin paramadharmiṣṭhe deśe bhūdoṣavarjite aṣṭādaśa samājagmur akṣauhiṇyo yuyutsayā
english: In that supremely righteous land, free from any taint of the earth, eighteen akṣauhiṇī armies assembled, eager for battle.

sanskrit: evaṃ nāmābhinirvṛttaṃ tasya deśasya vai dvijāḥ puṇyaś ca ramaṇīyaś ca sa deśo vaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
english: Thus, O twice-born, has the name of that region come about; and that holy and delightful land has now been described to you.

sanskrit: tad etat kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mayā vo munisattamāḥ yathā deśaḥ sa vikhyātas triṣu lokeṣu viśrutaḥ
english: All this has been told to you by me, O best of sages — how that region has become renowned and celebrated in the three worlds.

sanskrit: ṛṣaya ūcuḥ akṣauhiṇya iti proktaṃ yat tvayā sūtanandana etad icchāmahe śrotuṃ sarvam eva yathātatham
english: The sages said: O son of the sūta, you have used the word 'akṣauhiṇī' — we wish to hear all about that in full and exactly as it is.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyāḥ parīmāṇaṃ rathāśvanaradantinām yathāvac caiva no brūhi sarvaṃ hi viditaṃ tava
english: Tell us precisely the measure of an akṣauhiṇī in terms of chariots, horses, men and elephants — for all of this is known to you.

sanskrit: sūta uvāca eko ratho gajaś caiko narāḥ pañca padātayaḥ trayaś ca turagās tajjñaiḥ pattir ity abhidhīyate
english: The Sūta said: One chariot, one elephant, five foot-soldiers and three horses — this unit, by those who know, is called a patti.

sanskrit: pattiṃ tu triguṇām etām āhuḥ senāmukhaṃ budhāḥ trīṇi senāmukhāny eko gulma ity abhidhīyate
english: This patti multiplied by three is called a senāmukha by the wise; three senāmukhas together are called one gulma.

sanskrit: trayo gulmā gaṇo nāma vāhinī tu gaṇās trayaḥ smṛtās tisras tu vāhinyaḥ pṛtaneti vicakṣaṇaiḥ
english: Three gulmas constitute a gaṇa; three gaṇas are remembered as a vāhinī; and three vāhinīs are called a pṛtanā by those with discernment.

sanskrit: camūs tu pṛtanās tisras tisraś camvas tv anīkinī anīkinīṃ daśaguṇāṃ prāhur akṣauhiṇīṃ budhāḥ
english: Three pṛtanās make a camū; three camūs make an anīkinī; and ten anīkinīs, the learned declare, constitute an akṣauhiṇī.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyāḥ prasaṃkhyānaṃ rathānāṃ dvijasattamāḥ saṃkhyāgaṇitatattvajñaiḥ sahasrāṇy ekaviṃśatiḥ
english: The precise count of chariots in an akṣauhiṇī, O best of the twice-born, as reckoned by those who know the truth of number and calculation, is twenty-one thousand —

sanskrit: śatāny upari caivāṣṭau tathā bhūyaś ca saptatiḥ gajānāṃ tu parīmāṇam etad evātra nirdiśet
english: — and eight hundred and seventy more; and the count of elephants is exactly this same number.

sanskrit: jñeyaṃ śatasahasraṃ tu sahasrāṇi tathā nava narāṇām api pañcāśac chatāni trīṇi cānaghāḥ
english: The number of men, O sinless ones, is to be known as one hundred thousand plus nine thousand and three hundred and fifty.

sanskrit: pañcaṣaṣṭisahasrāṇi tathāśvānāṃ śatāni ca daśottarāṇi ṣaṭ prāhur yathāvad iha saṃkhyayā
english: For horses they give the count, accurately reckoned, as sixty-five thousand and six hundred and ten.

sanskrit: etām akṣauhiṇīṃ prāhuḥ saṃkhyātattvavido janāḥ yāṃ vaḥ kathitavān asmi vistareṇa dvijottamāḥ
english: This is what those who know the truth of enumeration call an akṣauhiṇī — which I have now described to you in full detail, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: etayā saṃkhyayā hy āsan kurupāṇḍavasenayoḥ akṣauhiṇyo dvijaśreṣṭhāḥ piṇḍenāṣṭādaśaiva tāḥ
english: By this reckoning the combined forces of the Kuru and Pāṇḍava armies, O best of the twice-born, were in total exactly eighteen akṣauhiṇīs.

sanskrit: sametās tatra vai deśe tatraiva nidhanaṃ gatāḥ kauravān kāraṇaṃ kṛtvā kālenādbhutakarmaṇā
english: They assembled in that very region and met their destruction there, the Kauravas being made the instrument by time of wondrous deeds.

sanskrit: ahāni yuyudhe bhīṣmo daśaiva paramāstravit ahāni pañca droṇas tu rarakṣa kuruvāhinīm
english: Bhīṣma, the supreme master of weapons, fought for just ten days; Droṇa then commanded and protected the Kuru army for five days.

sanskrit: ahanī yuyudhe dve tu karṇaḥ parabalārdanaḥ śalyo 'rdhadivasaṃ tv āsīd gadāyuddham ataḥ param
english: Karṇa, crusher of enemy forces, fought for two days; Śalya held command for half a day; after that came the mace-fight.

sanskrit: tasyaiva tu dinasyānte hārdikyadrauṇigautamāḥ prasuptaṃ niśi viśvastaṃ jaghnur yaudhiṣṭhiraṃ balam
english: At the close of that very day, Kṛtavarman son of Hṛdika, Aśvatthāman son of Droṇa, and Kṛpa son of Gautama slaughtered the army of Yudhiṣṭhira while it slept trustingly in the night.

sanskrit: yat tu śaunakasatre te bhāratākhyānavistaram ākhyāsye tatra paulomam ākhyānaṃ cāditaḥ param
english: At the sacrifice of Śaunaka I shall narrate the extensive tale of the Bhārata; there also, before it, I shall first tell the story called Pauloma.

sanskrit: vicitrārthapadākhyānam anekasamayānvitam abhipannaṃ naraiḥ prājñair vairāgyam iva mokṣibhiḥ
english: That tale of diverse meanings and varied metres, approached by wise men as the liberated approach dispassion — that is the one I shall tell.
